headline: Data Engineer Salary USA 2026: Pay by Level, City and Skill
metaDescription: Data engineer salary USA 2026: entry $80K–$105K, senior $147K–$179K. Top cities San Francisco $205K, NYC $171K. Spark, dbt and Airflow premiums plus demand outlook.

sections.content:
Data engineering remains one of the best-paid software roles in the United States. In 2026, entry-level engineers earn roughly $80,000 to $105,000 in base pay, with national averages landing near $94,800. Mid-level engineers with a few years of experience make $119,000 to $150,000.

Senior data engineers earn $147,000 to $179,000 in base salary, and staff or principal engineers clear $220,000 in base pay alone. Total compensation tells an even bigger story: senior total comp runs $220,000 to $320,000, staff can reach $300,000 to $450,000, and FAANG packages frequently exceed $250,000. The national benchmark average sits around $131,800.
sections.title: 2026 salary bands: entry to staff level

sections.content:
Location still matters enormously. San Francisco remains the ceiling at about $205,000 on average, with senior Snowflake roles in the Bay Area reaching $185,000 to $230,000. New York and Seattle both average around $171,000, Washington DC about $162,000 and Austin roughly $150,000.

Remote US roles average $163,700, and big-data or scarcity roles resist the usual remote discount. Note that remote-only postings have dropped to around 2 percent, with hybrid as the default, and salaries stay anchored to the metro of record.
sections.title: Pay by city: San Francisco, New York, Seattle and remote

sections.content:
Not all skills pay equally. In a 2026 analysis of nearly 7,000 US postings with a median base of $128,300, Apache Spark added about $19,800, dbt added $11,700, Airflow $10,700 and Snowflake $6,700. Python and SQL are table stakes at roughly $130,000, while Kafka and streaming carry a growing premium.

The 2026 skill priority list starts with deep SQL and Python or PySpark, plus data modeling, one major cloud platform with AWS the most common, orchestration with Airflow or Dagster, dbt, and increasingly streaming with Kafka and data governance as AI workloads expand.
sections.title: Skills that command a premium: Spark, dbt, Airflow

sections.content:
The outlook is strong. The field employs more than 150,000 people in the US and added over 20,000 jobs in the past year, with Texas holding about 26 percent of postings and California 24 percent. The global data-engineering services market is estimated at $105 billion in 2026, heading toward $213 billion by 2031, driven by AI workloads.

There is a two-tier market, though: entry-level generalists with only Python and SQL face heavy competition, while senior engineers with streaming and cloud-architecture depth can clear $250,000 in total comp at major tech firms. Specializing early in streaming, orchestration and cloud architecture is the fastest route to the top bands.
